questions.q: Why should copper sulfate solution not be boiled to dryness?
options: Hydrated crystals would lose their water of crystallisation
questions.a: B) Hydrated crystals would lose their water of crystallisation. Boiling to dryness gives white anhydrous powder, not blue hydrated crystals.

questions.q: Why add copper oxide in excess when making copper sulfate?
questions.a: To use up all the acid

questions.q: Big question: what do examiners look for in a practical method answer?
questions.a: Clear ordered steps, named equipment, what is measured and how, controls, and safety.

questions.q: Describe how to carry out paper chromatography of food colourings.
questions.a: Pencil line near the bottom (1); spots of colourings on the line (1); stand in solvent below the line, lid on (1); remove when solvent near top, mark solvent front, dry (1).
questions.model: Four steps, four marks: pencil line, spots, solvent below the line with a lid, mark the front and dry.

questions.q: Why is the solvent level below the start line?
questions.a: So the spots do not dissolve into the solvent in the beaker.

questions.q: State one safety precaution when heating magnesium.
questions.a: Eye protection; do not look directly at the flame; use tongs; heatproof mat.

questions.q: Describe how to find the empirical formula of magnesium oxide by experiment. Portal response box.
questions.a: Weigh crucible and lid (1); add Mg ribbon, weigh (1); heat strongly, lifting lid occasionally (1); heat to constant mass (1); cool and weigh (1); calculate masses of Mg and O and convert to moles (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two points: 'Weigh an empty crucible and lid. Add a coiled piece of cleaned magnesium ribbon and weigh again.'

questions.q: Describe how to show that a sample of water is pure.
questions.a: Heat and measure the boiling point (1); pure water boils at exactly 100 °C (1) at standard pressure; (freezes at 0 °C) (1).

questions.q: Explain why the volume of air decreases when iron wool rusts in an enclosed tube.
questions.a: Iron reacts with oxygen (1), removing it from the air, so the gas volume falls by about 21% (1).
